candidate_relations.reason: A gastric adenomatous polyp is a dysplastic epithelial neoplasm, not a gastric adenomyoma composed of glandular and smooth-muscle elements.
High-grade dysplasia denotes advanced epithelial atypia within a polyp and does not identify the referenced benign gastric adenomyoma.
Gastric adenomyoma is commonly regarded as a hamartomatous lesion, but gastric hamartoma omits the required adenomyoma subtype and glandular–smooth-muscle composition.
“None” does not correspond to the benchmark diagnosis of gastric adenomyoma.
Glandular hyperplasia may describe part of the glandular proliferation but omits the defining smooth-muscle component and adenomyoma diagnosis.
